evals.expected_output: An implemented, runnable React Three Fiber product configurator with the requested GLB, input, WebXR, accessible non-XR, mobile-quality, visual-regression, and CDN-delivery paths. The product/renderer contract and specialist routing support concrete source and build artifacts, measured acceptance evidence, and the actual delivery status; a routed plan alone does not complete the task.
assertions: The response uses threejs-development as the cross-cutting route instead of treating the request as one rendering effect.
Architecture, scene lifecycle, renderer, asset, and color ownership are established before optional advanced effects.
The WebXR experience has a usable non-XR and accessible path for essential product and purchase actions.
Mobile frame, memory, asset, DPR, and quality budgets are explicit and measured.
The implementation and evidence cover fixed visual baselines, production asset delivery, security controls, rollout, and rollback; proposed checks are distinguished from executed results.

Routing, pseudocode, a test plan, or unsupported claims of execution cannot earn a full task pass. Missing implementation or unavailable browser, GPU, XR, or authorized CDN-target evidence is reported as partial or blocked, with the specific unfinished requirements; it does not declare the configurator fully delivered or invent a deployment.

evals.prompt: Our GLB viewer leaks GPU memory every time the route changes, first interaction freezes while shaders compile, and corrupt customer-uploaded textures can crash the tab. Just increase the cache and keep all models alive.

It measures compilation and first-interaction behavior on the supplied viewer and validates any chosen warm-up or scheduling change. CPU submission time is not labeled GPU time, and an unreproduced stall is identified rather than invented.
Customer assets are validated for type, size, dimensions, counts, compression ratio, extensions, and parse or upload budgets.
Repeated mount and unmount tests show stable renderer and browser resource evidence.

It supplies source changes for the existing viewer, preserves shared resources while their owners remain active, and records actual inputs, commands, artifact identity and observed disposal/asset-failure behavior.

A route, advice, fabricated counters or a replacement demo cannot earn full task pass. Missing original inputs, unimplemented repairs, unavailable runtime evidence or unreproduced production symptoms remain explicit partial or blocked requirements.
